messages.author: 17944621d521fdfa
messages.subject: Single item - error variance
parts:
One of my latent variables is formed by 4 indicators, 2 of them are negatively worded therefore I reversed the scores. From an EFA the 2 reversed items form a distinct factor, I tried to keep them anyway but the CFA and then the SEM confirmed several problems in the model due to those two items (an inspection of the residual matrix confirmed me that).

So I dropped the two reversed items (I won't use reversed items never again in my life!)

The model works with two items that form the latent factor, but I know that a latent variable with only two indicators is not appropriate (unless any exceptions?).

I think the solution would be to use an aggregated measure of the two items, using the variable as observed, and constraining the error variance as suggested by Bollen (1989).

All this long story to ask you if the constraining should be specified as follow:

var ~~#*var

​
(where "#" is 1 - reliability). Is it correct?

When doing that, the model fit is not good anymore. Since the reliability I took from previous study does not reflect the exact same construct (items were a bit different in the meaning, and I did not found anything else closer), would be acceptable to keep the two items (var=~ item1 + item2)? I know this last question is not about Lavaan syntax but I would really appreciate your thoughts .

Thank you very much,

Fran

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Single item - error variance
parts:
Fran,

There are two main reasons to be concerned about only two items per factor.

The big one is identification. Generally speaking, a latent needs
three outgoing paths to be identified in the absence of additional
constraints. These can be to three or more indicators, or to two
indicators and an endogenous variable at the structural level.* In a
CFA, there is no structural level, so that's where the minimum of
three indicators comes from. Another possibility is additional
constraints. if your two items are from a scale and have comparable
metrics, it may be appropriate to constrain the two loadings to
equality.

The other big concern is that in a common-factor theory, you are
generally assuming that your indicators are representative of the
domain theoretically being measured. Depending on the domain and the
nature of the indicators, that may imply you want more. A small number
of homogenous items is measuring something relatively specific (which
may be what you want).

*You may have noticed the implication that the endogenous variable is
functioning much like an indicator. This is, in a sense, true,
especially if the structural relation is strong. This can be another
reason to have more indicators, to dilute this effect.

Pat

messages.subject: Re: Single item - error variance
parts:
var=~a1*item1 + a2*item2
#constraining the parameters
a1==a2

Yes, or you could assign the same labels:

var =~ a1*item1 + a1*item2

Or you could fix them both to 1 and estimate the factor variance:

var =~ 1*item1 + a*item2
var ~~ NA*var

messages.subject: Re: Single item - error variance
parts:
I got a similar problem with another dataset but I have one indicator only. I am running a CFA and a SEM model with both latent factors and single indicators. The question is how to include a single observed indicator into CFA and SEM on Lavaan.

I would like to have feedback on my syntax and possibly any theoretical advice. I am following Brown (2015) which suggests to fix the unstandardised error of the indicator to some predetermined value, created using the sample variance of the single indicator and the estimate reliability:

VAR(X)(1 –r)

VAR(X)= is the sample variance of the single indicator
r = is the reliability estimate of the indicator. 

There is no available scale that measures the same construct as mine, therefore I used the reliability of the closest construct I found in the literature. 

- Sample variance
var(df$my_variable)# 2.2

- Reliability from the closest construct = .94

- Value used to fix the error
2.2*(1-.94) # = .13

In the CFA and SEM my syntax for this indicator would be as follows:

myvar_latent=~ my_variable

my_variable~~.13*my_variable

Are these steps correct?


Thank you very much!

Fran

Brown, T. A. (2015). Confirmatory factor analysis for applied research. Guilford publications.
